description: Historical and contextual entities referenced by the novel. These entities are separate from the nine main characters and from the secondary fictional cast.

entities.name: Kobayakawa Hideaki
entities.summary: Daimyō and adopted member of the Toyotomi family. At Sekigahara in 1600 he defected from the Western Army and attacked Ōtani Yoshitsugu's forces, helping secure Tokugawa Ieyasu's victory.

entities.name: Ishida Mitsunari
entities.summary: Toyotomi administrator and one of the principal leaders of the Western coalition at Sekigahara. He commanded from Mount Sasao and was defeated by Tokugawa Ieyasu's coalition.

entities.name: Ukita Hideie
entities.summary: Daimyō and major Toyotomi ally who commanded a large contingent of the Western Army at Sekigahara. His forces fought in the center before the Western Army collapsed.

entities.name: Shimazu Yoshihiro
entities.summary: Daimyō of Satsuma and commander of the Shimazu contingent at Sekigahara. His forces initially remained inactive and later made a famous retreat through the Eastern Army.

entities.name: Konishi Yukinaga
entities.summary: Christian daimyō and Toyotomi commander who fought for the Western Army at Sekigahara. After the defeat he was captured and executed rather than committing suicide.

entities.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
entities.summary: Founder of the Tokugawa shogunate and leader of the Eastern Army at Sekigahara. His victory in 1600 enabled him to consolidate political control over Japan.

entities.name: Battle of Sekigahara
entities.summary: Decisive battle between the Eastern coalition led by Tokugawa Ieyasu and the Western coalition associated with the Toyotomi cause. The Western Army's defeat transformed the balance of power in Japan.

entities.name: Eastern Army
entities.summary: Coalition led by Tokugawa Ieyasu during the Sekigahara campaign of 1600.

entities.name: Western Army
entities.summary: Coalition formed around the Toyotomi cause and led operationally at Sekigahara by Ishida Mitsunari and other allied commanders.
